questions.stem: Which four activities form the commonly used emergency-management cycle?
options: Plan, purchase, punish, and promote
Inspect, cite, appeal, and close
Hire, train, transfer, and retire
Prevention or mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Emergency management reduces likelihood and consequence, prepares capabilities, manages the event, and restores operations and communities.
incorrectOptionExplanations: These are unrelated management actions.
These describe enforcement steps, not emergency management.
These are workforce lifecycle actions.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)

questions.stem: Which item belongs in an emergency action plan?
options: Procedures for reporting, evacuation, accountability, critical operations, rescue or medical duties, and contacts
Only the annual safety budget
Only a list of production targets
Only the insurance policy number
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: An EAP establishes who does what, how emergencies are reported, how people evacuate or shelter, and how accountability and assistance are managed.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Budget may support resources but is not the emergency procedure itself.
Production targets do not direct protective action.
Insurance information does not replace reporting, evacuation, accountability, and roles.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, emergency action plan components, pp. 874-877; OSHA 1910.38

questions.stem: A drill shows that supervisors cannot account for contractors and visitors. What is the strongest correction?
options: Count employees only
Integrate visitor and contractor rosters, assembly assignments, and reconciliation into the accountability process
Ask visitors to call later if safe
Stop recording visitors at entry
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Accountability must include all people on site and link entry records, assembly areas, supervisors, and escalation for missing persons.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Everyone under site responsibility should be considered in emergency accountability.
Delayed self-reporting is unreliable during a developing emergency.
Removing entry records makes accountability harder.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, accounting for employees after evacuation, pp. 875-877

questions.stem: A toxic outdoor plume is moving across the only evacuation route. Which protective action may be preferable if the building can be secured?
options: Evacuate everyone directly through the plume
Open outside-air intakes to dilute indoor air
Shelter in place using the preplanned isolation and communication procedure
Let each employee choose an uncoordinated route
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Protective action should be based on hazard location, duration, building protection, routes, and emergency authority rather than assuming evacuation is always safest.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Movement through a toxic plume can increase exposure.
Outside-air intake may draw the contaminant indoors.
Uncoordinated decisions undermine accountability and protective strategy.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, chemical spills, evacuation, and emergency planning considerations, pp. 874-880

questions.stem: Which emergency communication system is most resilient?
options: One untested email list
A single alarm that has the same signal for every event
Informal word of mouth only
Multiple tested methods with clear messages, backups, ownership, and accommodations for affected populations
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Redundant channels and predefined messages improve speed, reach, accessibility, and reliability under disrupted conditions.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Email can fail due to power, network, access, or outdated lists.
Different hazards may require distinct protective actions and understandable signals.
Word of mouth is slow, incomplete, and difficult to verify.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, reporting emergencies, crisis management, and continuity communications, pp. 874-888

questions.stem: A site has never tested its emergency plan. What is the best first exercise progression?
options: Begin with a facilitated tabletop, correct gaps, then progress to functional and full-scale exercises
Begin with an unannounced full-scale event involving every hazard
Review the plan silently and call it an exercise
Wait for a real emergency
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Progressive exercises build knowledge and complexity while allowing findings to be corrected between stages.
incorrectOptionExplanations: An immediate complex exercise can create uncontrolled risk and poor learning when roles are untested.
Reading a document does not test coordination and decisions.
Real events are not safe substitutes for planned validation.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, emergency planning and preparedness, pp. 870-889

questions.stem: A facility relies on the local fire department for hazardous-material response. What is needed before an emergency?
options: Assume the department knows the process
Coordinate hazards, access, capabilities, contacts, water supply, command, and exercise expectations
Call for the first time during the release
Provide only the facility street address
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Mutual-aid arrangements should be planned, documented, shared, and tested so outside resources integrate with site command.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Responders may not know chemicals, layout, isolation, or site resources.
First-time coordination during an event wastes time and increases uncertainty.
An address is necessary but insufficient for effective preplanning.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, emergency planning, contacts, and response coordination, pp. 870-889

questions.stem: What is the main output of a business impact analysis for continuity planning?
options: A list of every employee favorite task
Only the replacement cost of the building
Prioritized essential functions, dependencies, impacts, and recovery time requirements
A guarantee that no disruption will occur
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A BIA identifies what must continue or recover, by when, and which people, information, facilities, suppliers, and technology it depends on.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Personal preferences do not define organizational continuity needs.
Property value is one impact and does not identify essential services or dependencies.
Continuity planning manages disruption; it cannot guarantee prevention.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, business continuity planning and plan components, pp. 885-888; FEMA continuity toolkit

questions.stem: What does a recovery time objective describe?
options: The probability that an emergency will occur
The amount of chemical that may be released
The annual training attendance goal
The targeted maximum time to restore a function after disruption
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: RTO guides continuity strategies and resources by defining how quickly an essential process should be restored.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Likelihood is part of risk assessment, not recovery timing.
Release quantity is a hazard scenario input.
Training attendance is a program metric, not the function recovery target.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, business continuity plan components, pp. 885-888

questions.stem: Two departments issue conflicting evacuation and shutdown instructions during a release. What system weakness is most evident?
options: Command authority, roles, and communication were not clearly established
The event needed more independent decision makers
Emergency plans should avoid defined leadership
Each department should use a separate alarm
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: An incident-management structure aligns authority, objectives, information, operations, and external coordination.
incorrectOptionExplanations: More independent commands can increase conflict and delay.
Defined leadership and responsibilities are essential for coordinated response.
Separate uncoordinated alarms can confuse protective actions.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, emergency management, crisis management, and response organization, pp. 870-888

questions.stem: What should an after-action review produce?
options: A celebration only
Evidence-based strengths, gaps, assigned corrective actions, due dates, and effectiveness follow-up
A confidential list of people to blame
A revised plan with no training or retest
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: After-action learning should convert observations into owned, verified improvements to plans, resources, training, and coordination.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Recognition may be appropriate but does not capture learning.
Blame discourages reporting and often misses system causes.
A document change alone does not establish implementation or capability.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, preparedness, response, recovery, and continuity, pp. 870-889

questions.stem: Which event should trigger review of an emergency plan before the normal review date?
options: Only a change in company logo
Only a change in cafeteria menu
A significant process, facility, staffing, hazard, contact, or regulatory change
Only the end of a calendar decade
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Plans must remain aligned with current hazards, people, facilities, resources, contacts, and external arrangements.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Branding may require formatting updates but not necessarily emergency capability changes.
Menu changes generally do not alter the emergency basis unless they introduce relevant hazards.
Review should respond to risk and organizational change, not an arbitrary decade.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 39, emergency planning requirements and continuity maintenance, pp. 870-889
